# remove-markdown 0.8.1

This patch fixes a case where HTML stripping could delete part of a sentence.
In 0.8.0, `5 < 10 and 10 > 5` became `5  5`. Version 0.8.1 keeps the full
comparison, including when it appears between HTML tags.

```js
const removeMd = require('remove-markdown');

removeMd('5 < 10 and 10 > 5');        // '5 < 10 and 10 > 5'
removeMd('<b>2 < 3</b>');              // '2 < 3'
removeMd('low <= limit and high > 0'); // 'low <= limit and high > 0'
```

The fix applies by default and with `htmlTagsToSkip`. It recognizes a space
or tab before `<` or `<=` and whitespace after the operator. The same spacing
also preserves text like `Keep < label > here`. Compact expressions such as
`5<10 and 10>5` still produce `55`.

Of the 40 project fixtures, only the comparison example changed. All 652
CommonMark 0.31.2 examples produced the same output as before. In a sample of
301 dependency Markdown files, 15 recovered text that 0.8.0 had dropped.
The pull request includes the full compatibility results. [PR #144](https://github.com/zuchka/remove-markdown/pull/144)

Thanks to @gnapse for reporting the comparison case in [issue #55](https://github.com/zuchka/remove-markdown/issues/55).

```sh
npm install remove-markdown@0.8.1
```
